title: Constitutional Ai Rlaif

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: RLHF needs labelers. Labelers are slow, biased, and expensive. You can eliminate a labeler by replacing them with a model that reads explicit principles. The first formal version of this substitution was Bai et al.'s Constitutional AI. It worked well enough that every frontier lab now uses some variant of AI-feedback post-training.

The catch: the preference signal is now generated by the same class of model you are training. Biases in the labeler (now: in the principles plus the labeler model's interpretation) can be amplified rather than attenuated. Lesson 4's sycophancy argument still applies; the labeler just moved inside the loop.
